exams.name: Head-to-Toe Screening
exams.summary: The full-body objective screen, worked through system by system. Every other exam in this section is a focused expansion of one of these blocks.
exams.script: Introduce yourself, say you have just washed your hands, describe what the exam will cover, and ask for consent before touching the patient. Tell them they may stop you at any point.

steps.how: Observe as the patient comes in and settles: level of distress, dress appropriate to the weather and occasion, grooming, posture, and whether communication is intact.
steps.normal: A [age]-year-old [sex] with no signs of distress, dressed appropriately for the weather and occasion, with communication intact.

steps.how: Inspect the head and face for symmetry. Have the patient raise the brows, close the eyes tightly, smile and puff the cheeks to test facial nerve motor function.
steps.normal: Head and face are normal with facial symmetry and intact motor function of the facial nerve bilaterally.

steps.how: Inspect and palpate the skull for shape, lesions and evidence of trauma.
steps.normal: The head is normocephalic and atraumatic.

steps.how: Inspect the lips for colour, moisture, lesions and rashes.
steps.normal: Lips are without cyanosis or rashes.

steps.how: Inspect the lids, lashes and periorbital tissue for exudate, erythema, oedema and ptosis.
steps.normal: Eyes are normal without signs of exudate, erythema or ptosis.

steps.how: Retract the lower lid and inspect the palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva and the sclera for injection, pallor and icterus.
steps.normal: Conjunctiva and sclera are non-injected and without scleral icterus.
steps.flag: The source notes read “noninjected with yellow appearance.” A yellow sclera is icterus — an abnormal finding — so this is recorded here as the normal negative it was meant to be.

steps.how: Palpate and, if indicated, transilluminate the frontal and maxillary sinuses.
steps.normal: Frontal and maxillary sinuses are non-tender to palpation.

steps.how: Inspect the external nose for erythema, discharge and an allergic crease.
steps.normal: The external nose is non-erythematous with no creasing or discharge.

steps.how: Inspect and palpate the pinna, tragus and mastoid bilaterally.
steps.normal: Ears are symmetrical bilaterally with non-tender pinna, tragus and mastoid.

steps.how: Place a finger at each tragus and have the patient open and close the jaw; feel for crepitus, clicking, popping and locking.
steps.normal: TMJ is non-tender without crepitus, locking or popping.

steps.how: Palpate the masseter and temporalis with the teeth clenched.
steps.normal: Motor function of the trigeminal nerve is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Palpate the preauricular, postauricular, tonsillar, submandibular, submental, anterior cervical, posterior cervical and occipital chains.
steps.normal: No lymphadenopathy is observed in the preauricular, postauricular, tonsillar, submandibular, submental, anterior cervical, posterior cervical or occipital regions.

steps.how: Palpate the isthmus and lobes from in front or behind while the patient swallows.
steps.normal: Thyroid is non-palpable without nodules.

steps.how: Shrug the shoulders and turn the head against resistance.
steps.normal: The accessory nerve is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Snellen chart at distance, both eyes together (OU), with correction if worn.
steps.normal: Vision is 20/20 OU without correction.

steps.how: Test direct and consensual light response and accommodation.
steps.normal: PERRLA is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Follow a fingertip through an H pattern using the eyes only; watch for lid lag and nystagmus.
steps.normal: EOMI are normal without nystagmus.

steps.how: Bring a target toward the bridge of the nose and watch both eyes converge.
steps.normal: Convergence is symmetric bilaterally.

steps.how: Darken the room; examine the disc, cup-to-disc ratio, vessels and macula in each eye.
steps.normal: Fundoscopic exam reveals a 1:2 cup-to-disc ratio without cupping, AV nicking, cotton-wool spots or papilloedema.

steps.how: Occlude one ear; present a sound and withdraw it, or use a whispered word at arm's length.
steps.normal: Gross hearing is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Straighten the canal, inspect the canal and the tympanic membrane for landmarks, colour and mobility.
steps.normal: The external auditory canal is patent, non-erythematous and without exudate, cerumen or discharge. Tympanic membranes are intact and non-boggy bilaterally.

steps.how: Inspect the septum, turbinates and mucosa with a speculum or otoscope tip.
steps.normal: The nasal septum is midline without deviation, and the nasal mucosa is moist and non-erythematous without polyps or discharge.

steps.how: Inspect the buccal mucosa, gingivae, tongue and teeth.
steps.normal: The oral mucosa is moist and without nodules. Teeth are intact without dental caries.

steps.how: Depress the tongue and have the patient say “ahh”; inspect the pharynx, tonsils, uvula and palate rise.
steps.normal: The posterior oropharynx is non-erythematous without exudate. Tonsils are +2 bilaterally. The uvula and tongue are midline. Cranial nerves IX, X and XII are intact.

steps.how: Inspect the thorax for shape, symmetry, accessory muscle use and cyanosis, comparing anteroposterior with transverse diameter.
steps.normal: The thoracic wall has a 2:1 transverse-to-AP ratio with symmetry and no signs of cyanosis.
steps.flag: The source reads “2:1 A/P ratio.” The normal adult chest is about twice as wide as it is deep — transverse:AP of roughly 2:1, i.e. AP:transverse of 1:2. A ratio approaching 1:1 is a barrel chest.

steps.how: Diaphragm, patient breathing through an open mouth; compare side to side over the apices and the posterior and lateral fields.
steps.normal: Lungs are clear to auscultation in the apices and the posterior and lateral lung fields, without wheezing, rhonchi or rales.

steps.how: Bell over each carotid with the patient holding their breath; never palpate both at once.
steps.normal: There are no bruits in the carotid arteries.

steps.how: Auscultate the aortic, pulmonic, tricuspid and mitral points with diaphragm and bell.
steps.normal: The heart has a regular rate and rhythm at the cardiac points without abnormal sounds.

steps.how: Palpate for the apical impulse and locate it by interspace and line.
steps.normal: The PMI is midclavicular in the 5th intercostal space.

steps.how: Auscultate all four quadrants before percussing or palpating.
steps.normal: Bowel sounds are positive in all four quadrants.

steps.how: Bell over the abdominal aorta and the renal and iliac arteries.
steps.normal: No bruits are noted in the abdominal aorta or the renal and iliac arteries.

steps.how: Percuss the four quadrants for the distribution of tympany and dullness.
steps.normal: Percussion of the abdomen reveals scattered dullness with tympany.

steps.how: Light then deep palpation of all quadrants, tender area last; feel for the liver and spleen edges.
steps.normal: The abdomen is non-tender and without masses. There are no signs of hepatosplenomegaly.

steps.how: Palpate the head and neck chains, then the supraclavicular and infraclavicular fossae.
steps.normal: No lymphadenopathy is observed in the preauricular, postauricular, tonsillar, submandibular, submental, anterior cervical, posterior cervical, occipital, supraclavicular or infraclavicular regions.

steps.how: Watch the patient walk away and back.
steps.normal: Gait is intact.

steps.how: Feet together, eyes closed for 30 seconds; then arms held forward and supinated, eyes closed.
steps.normal: Romberg and pronator drift tests are negative.

steps.how: Inspect the joints and the standing spine, including forward flexion for a rib hump.
steps.normal: Joints are normal in appearance without signs of scoliosis.

steps.how: Active cervical and lumbar flexion, extension, lateral flexion and rotation.
steps.normal: Cervical and lumbar active range of motion are within normal limits.

steps.how: Heel-to-shin and point-to-point testing.
steps.normal: Heel-to-shin and point-to-point tests are well coordinated.

steps.how: Biceps, brachioradialis, triceps, patellar and Achilles; grade 0–4.
steps.normal: Deep tendon reflexes for the biceps, brachioradialis, triceps, patellar and Achilles are +2 bilaterally.

steps.how: Inspect and palpate the face and the upper and lower extremities for texture, turgor, pigmentation and lesions.
steps.normal: Inspection of the skin on the face and the upper and lower extremities reveals normal texture, turgor and pigmentation. There are no signs of petechiae, rashes, nodules or cyanosis.

steps.how: Inspect the nail plate, bed and profile angle.
steps.normal: Nails are normal in size without clubbing.

steps.how: Inspect distribution, the scalp and the shafts.
steps.normal: Hair shows normal distribution with no signs of alopecia, flaking, nodules or lice.

findings.finding: Scleral icterus
findings.suggests: Hyperbilirubinaemia — hepatocellular disease, biliary obstruction or haemolysis

findings.finding: Conjunctival pallor
Sinus tenderness with purulent discharge and a blocked nose
Bulging, immobile or erythematous tympanic membrane
Non-tender, hard, fixed supraclavicular node (Virchow's)
Tender, mobile cervical nodes with a sore throat
findings.suggests: Reactive lymphadenopathy — viral or streptococcal pharyngitis

findings.finding: Diffusely enlarged thyroid or a discrete nodule
findings.suggests: Goitre, thyroiditis or thyroid nodule — test TSH and image

findings.finding: Papilloedema
AV nicking, copper wiring, cotton-wool spots
Increased AP diameter approaching 1:1 (barrel chest)
Expiratory wheeze
Fine late-inspiratory crackles at the bases
Carotid bruit
PMI displaced laterally and inferiorly
Digital clubbing
findings.suggests: Chronic hypoxia, bronchiectasis, lung malignancy, cirrhosis, IBD

exams.name: Abdominal Exam
exams.summary: The four-quadrant abdominal exam in sequence — inspect, auscultate, percuss, palpate — with organ borders and the appendicitis manoeuvre.
exams.script: Patient supine with the arms at the sides and the knees slightly flexed to relax the abdominal wall. Warm your hands, expose from the xiphoid to the pubic symphysis, and ask them to point to where it hurts before you touch — that quadrant is palpated last.

steps.how: Stand at the patient's right and inspect tangentially across the abdomen.
steps.normal: Upon inspection, the abdomen appears flat, symmetric and without signs of distension.

steps.how: Inspect for discoloration, rashes, scars, dilated veins, masses and striae.
steps.normal: No signs of discoloration, rashes, scars, venous network, masses or striae.

steps.how: Inspect position, contour and any herniation or discharge.
steps.normal: Umbilicus is midline.

steps.how: Watch for visible peristalsis and aortic pulsation.
steps.normal: No signs of peristalsis or aortic pulsation visualized.

steps.how: Ask the patient to raise the head off the table or perform a Valsalva manoeuvre; watch the midline, umbilicus and any scars.
steps.normal: Upon Valsalva manoeuvre, no signs of hernias.

groups.name: Auscultation

steps.how: Diaphragm with light pressure in all four quadrants; before calling bowel sounds absent, listen in one spot for up to five minutes.
steps.normal: All four quadrants reveal normal bowel sounds, with no signs of hyperactive or hypoactive sounds.

steps.how: Bell over the abdominal aorta and the renal, iliac and femoral arteries.
steps.normal: No bruits heard upon auscultation of the abdominal aorta and the renal, iliac and femoral arteries.

groups.note: Auscultate before you percuss or palpate — handling the abdomen first alters bowel sounds.

steps.how: Percuss each quadrant, noting the distribution of tympany and dullness.
steps.normal: Percussion of the four quadrants revealed tympany with scattered dullness.

steps.how: Percuss down the right midclavicular line from lung resonance to dullness, then up from abdominal tympany; measure between the two.
steps.normal: The liver is within normal limits between 6 and 12 cm in size and is on the right midclavicular line.

steps.how: Percuss Traube's space and the lowest intercostal space in the left anterior axillary line before and after inspiration.
steps.normal: The spleen is within normal limits and is on the left midaxillary line.

steps.how: Light palpation of all four quadrants first, then deep; the painful quadrant last.
steps.normal: Upon light and deep palpation, no signs of pain or tenderness, guarding or rigidity noted. No signs of masses or fluids.

steps.how: Hand below the right costal margin; ask for a deep breath and feel the edge descend.
steps.normal: Palpation of the edge of the liver revealed a smooth and non-tender border at the costal margin, revealing no hepatosplenomegaly.
steps.flag: The source reads “costovertebral margin.” The liver edge is felt at the costal margin; the costovertebral angle is where the kidney is percussed.

steps.how: Reach over from the patient's right, cup the left lower ribs, and feel below the left costal margin on inspiration.
steps.normal: The spleen was non-palpable and no tenderness or masses were noted in the left midaxillary region, revealing no splenomegaly.

steps.how: Press deeply just left of the midline above the umbilicus and judge the width of the pulsation.
steps.normal: The abdominal aorta was palpable but no tenderness, masses or abnormal pulsations were palpated or visualized.

steps.how: Palpate one third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.
steps.normal: McBurney's point is non-tender, revealing no signs of appendicitis.

findings.finding: Absent bowel sounds after five minutes of listening
findings.suggests: Paralytic ileus or late bowel obstruction

findings.finding: High-pitched rushes and tinkling
Bruit over the aorta or a renal artery
Widened, expansile pulsation greater than about 3 cm
Liver span greater than 12 cm at the midclavicular line
Palpable spleen tip
findings.suggests: Splenomegaly — portal hypertension, haematological or infectious cause

findings.finding: Flank dullness that shifts with position
Involuntary guarding, rigidity or rebound tenderness
Tenderness at McBurney's point with a positive Rovsing, psoas or obturator sign
Inspiratory arrest on right subcostal palpation (Murphy's sign)
Costovertebral angle tenderness
Periumbilical (Cullen's) or flank (Grey Turner's) ecchymosis
Dilated periumbilical veins (caput medusae)
Reducible bulge appearing on Valsalva

exams.name: Cervical Spine and TMJ
exams.summary: Head carriage, cervical inspection and palpation, cervical range of motion and strength, and the temporomandibular joint.
exams.script: “Hello, my name is ___ and I will be your student clinician today. I have just finished washing my hands and we will be starting with a musculoskeletal exam. If at any point you have a question, please stop me and we will assess from there. Do I have your consent to continue?”

steps.how: Patient seated; inspect head position in relation to the axial skeleton.
steps.normal: Head is midline with no anterior head carriage.

steps.how: Inspect for abnormalities, antalgic position, oedema, colour, symmetry and curvature.
steps.normal: No abnormal curvature, atrophy or antalgic position noted.

steps.how: Palpate the occiput, axis, cervical spinous processes, facets and musculature, noting alignment, pain and heat.
steps.normal: Cervical spine is inspected and palpated without tenderness, abnormal colour, oedema or heat; no masses, misalignment or effusion noted. Occiput, axis, cervical spinous processes and facets are free from swelling and crepitus.

steps.how: Flexion and extension, rotation, lateral flexion — active first, then passive.
steps.normal: Active and passive range of motion of cervical flexion/extension, rotation and lateral flexion are within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain.

steps.how: Resist flexion and extension, rotation and lateral flexion; grade each 0–5.
steps.normal: Muscle strength and tone of cervical flexion/extension, lateral flexion and rotation are intact, grade +5.

steps.how: Inspect the jaw as the patient opens and closes, watching for swelling and deviation. Palpate at the tragus and external auditory canal and feel the condyle move, noting crepitus, clicking and popping.
steps.normal: No popping, locking, clicking, crepitus or pain noted on palpation. No swelling noted.

findings.finding: Anterior head carriage with rounded shoulders
findings.suggests: Upper-crossed postural pattern — deep neck flexor weakness

findings.finding: Loss of cervical lordosis with an antalgic head position
Midline cervical spinous tenderness after trauma
Arm pain reproduced by extension, rotation and axial load (Spurling's)
Neck pain with fever and neck stiffness on passive flexion
Jaw click with deviation that corrects on opening
Limited opening with locking and no click
Crepitus on jaw movement

exams.name: Thoracic and Lumbar Spine
exams.summary: Spinal movement in gait, palpation and percussion of the spinous processes and facets, and thoracolumbar range of motion and strength.
exams.script: “Hello, my name is ___ and I will be your student clinician today. I have just finished washing my hands and we will be starting with a musculoskeletal exam. If at any point you have a question, please stop me and we will assess from there. Do I have your consent to continue?”

steps.how: Instruct the patient to walk to the wall and back, observing the whole body while walking.
steps.normal: Gait is intact with no abnormalities. Neck and trunk are in line.

steps.how: Patient standing; palpate and percuss the spinous processes and palpate the facet joints of each vertebra along the spine, noting alignment, joint deformity, symmetry, colour, oedema, masses and pain.
steps.normal: Inspection, palpation and percussion of the thoracic, lumbar and sacroiliac spine bilaterally reveals proper alignment, no joint deformity, antalgic position, asymmetry, effusion, rubor, heat, tenderness or evidence of masses.

steps.how: Thoracic and lumbar flexion and extension, lateral flexion and rotation.
steps.normal: Active and passive ROM of the thoracic and lumbar spine for flexion/extension, lateral flexion and rotation are within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain.

steps.how: Resist thoracic and lumbar flexion and extension, lateral flexion and rotation; grade each 0–5.
steps.normal: Muscle strength and tone of thoracic and lumbar flexion/extension, lateral flexion and rotation are intact, grade +5.

findings.finding: Lateral curvature with a rib hump on forward flexion
Exaggerated thoracic kyphosis with loss of height
Point percussion tenderness over a spinous process
Saddle anaesthesia, bladder or bowel change, bilateral leg weakness
Leg pain reproduced by straight-leg raise at 30–70°
Positive FABER or thigh thrust
Morning stiffness over 30 minutes that eases with movement, reduced Schober
Back pain with fever, night pain or unexplained weight loss
findings.suggests: Infection or malignancy — image before treating

exams.name: Upper Extremities
exams.summary: Shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand — inspection, joint palpation, range of motion against resistance, and grip strength.
exams.script: “Hello, my name is ___ and I will be your student clinician today. I have just finished washing my hands and we will be starting with a musculoskeletal exam. If at any point you have a question, please stop me and we will assess from there. Do I have your consent to continue?”

steps.how: Instruct the patient to walk to the wall and back, observing arm position and swing.
steps.normal: Upper extremities are of normal motion upon walking and at rest.

steps.how: Patient seated; inspect each joint for deformity, antalgic position, asymmetry, atrophy, oedema, colour and masses.
steps.normal: Inspection of upper extremity joints bilaterally reveals no joint deformity, antalgic position, asymmetry, atrophy, oedema, abnormal colour or evidence of masses.

steps.how: Inspect the palms for muscle bulk and wasting.
steps.normal: Thenar and hypothenar eminences are prominent, no atrophy noted.

steps.how: Palpate the anterior and posterior shoulder, the glenohumeral, sternoclavicular and acromioclavicular joints, the olecranon process, the epicondyles, the radial and ulnar attachments, and the carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
steps.normal: Upper extremity joints palpated without tenderness, oedema or heat; no masses, misalignment or effusion.

steps.how: Ask the patient to place their hands out; compress across the MCP joints, then palpate the PIP and DIP joints medially and laterally.
steps.normal: No tenderness or pain upon compression.

steps.how: Active, passive and resisted flexion and extension, abduction and adduction, internal and external rotation.
steps.normal: Active and passive range of motion of shoulder abduction/adduction, flexion/extension and internal/external rotation within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain. Muscle strength and tone of shoulder abduction/adduction, flexion/extension and internal/external rotation intact, grade +5.

steps.how: Active, passive and resisted elbow flexion and extension, forearm pronation and supination, wrist flexion, extension and ulnar/radial deviation, finger flexion, extension, abduction and adduction, and thumb opposition.
steps.normal: Active, passive and resistant range of motion shows thumb flexion/extension and abduction/adduction, finger flexion/extension, wrist ulnar/radial deviation, wrist flexion/extension, pronation/supination of the forearm and elbow flexion/extension within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain. Muscle strength and tone of finger abduction/adduction, wrist flexion/extension, pronation/supination of the forearm and elbow flexion/extension intact, grade +5.

steps.how: Offer two fingers and instruct the patient to wrap their hand around and squeeze tightly three times.
steps.normal: Grip strength ×3 is intact bilaterally.

findings.finding: Painful arc between 60° and 120° of abduction, positive empty-can
Positive Hawkins-Kennedy or Neer
AC joint tenderness with a positive cross-body adduction test
Global loss of both active and passive shoulder motion
Lateral epicondyle tenderness on resisted wrist extension
Thenar atrophy with a positive Phalen or Tinel sign
findings.suggests: Median nerve compression — carpal tunnel syndrome

findings.finding: Symmetric MCP and PIP synovitis with over an hour of morning stiffness
Bony enlargement of the DIP joints (Heberden's nodes)
Acutely hot, red, exquisitely tender joint
findings.suggests: Septic arthritis or crystal arthropathy — aspirate

exams.name: Lower Extremities
exams.summary: Hip, knee, ankle and foot — gait observation, joint inspection and palpation, and range of motion against resistance.
exams.script: “Hello, my name is ___ and I will be your student clinician today. I have just finished washing my hands and we will be starting with a musculoskeletal exam. If at any point you have a question, please stop me and we will assess from there. Do I have your consent to continue?”

steps.how: Instruct the patient to walk from one wall to the other; observe gait and body position.
steps.normal: No signs of misalignment or asymmetries upon motion or at rest.

steps.how: Inspect the hip, knee, ankle and foot for deformity, antalgic position, asymmetry, effusion, rubor, heat and masses.
steps.normal: Inspection of lower extremity joints (knee, ankle, foot) bilaterally reveals no joint deformity, antalgic position, asymmetry, effusion, rubor, heat or evidence of masses.

steps.how: Palpate the hip, sacroiliac joint, patella, patellofemoral ligament, knee MCL and LCL, bursae, ankle, talofibular ligament, Achilles tendon, calcaneus, plantar fascia, MTP joints and the PIP and DIP joints.
steps.normal: Lower extremity joints (knee, ankle, foot) palpated without tenderness, oedema or heat; no masses, misalignment or effusion palpated.

steps.how: Patient supine for flexion, abduction and adduction, and internal and external rotation; side-lying for extension. Active, passive and resisted at each.
steps.normal: Active, passive and resistant ROM of hip flexion/extension, hip abduction/adduction and hip internal/external rotation within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain.

steps.how: Active, passive and resisted knee flexion and extension, ankle flexion and extension, ankle eversion and inversion, and toe flexion and extension.
steps.normal: Active, passive and resistant ROM of knee flexion/extension, ankle flexion/extension, ankle eversion/inversion and toe flexion/extension within normal limits without crepitus, contracture or pain.

findings.finding: Antalgic gait — shortened stance phase on one side
findings.suggests: Pain avoidance on the affected limb

findings.finding: Pelvis drops on the unsupported side (Trendelenburg)
Loss of internal rotation and groin pain
Knee effusion with a positive ballottement or bulge sign
Positive Lachman or anterior drawer
Joint line tenderness with a positive McMurray
Absent plantarflexion on calf squeeze (Thompson's test)
Heel pain worst on the first steps of the day with medial calcaneal tenderness
Unilateral calf swelling, warmth and tenderness
Hot, swollen, exquisitely tender single joint with fever
Podagra — acute first MTP pain, redness and swelling

exams.name: Neurological Exam
exams.summary: Level of consciousness, all twelve cranial nerves, motor and sensory function, deep tendon reflexes, cerebellar coordination, and gait and balance.
exams.script: “Today we’ll be doing a neurological exam, where I check how your brain and body are communicating — strength, balance and sensation. I’ll tell you what I’m doing at each step, and you can pause or stop at any time. I have just washed my hands — do I have your consent to continue?”

steps.how: Ask for their full name, where they are, and the date or day of the week.
steps.normal: Patient is alert and orientated ×3.

groups.name: Cranial nerves

steps.how: Eyes closed, one nostril occluded; identify a familiar, non-noxious scent, then repeat on the other side.
steps.normal: Olfaction is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Snellen chart at distance and the Rosenbaum card at near, both eyes (OU). Then visual fields by confrontation: demonstrate the difference between a moving and a still hand, cover one eye, and ask them to say which they see in each quadrant.
steps.normal: Visual acuity is 20/20 OU. Visual fields are intact bilaterally by confrontation.

steps.how: Cover one eye and then the other. Measure pupil size against a pupil card and test the direct and consensual light response and accommodation with a penlight.
steps.normal: PERRLA, with pupil size measured at around 3 mm.

steps.step: CN III, IV and VI — extraocular movements
steps.how: Ask the patient to follow your fingertip through an H pattern using the eyes only, without moving the head. Watch for lid lag and for nystagmus at the end points.
steps.normal: Extraocular movements are intact bilaterally without signs of lid lag or nystagmus.
steps.flag: The source notes number the cranial nerves in the order they are performed, so trochlear and abducens appear there as “4.” They are cranial nerves IV and VI, and are tested together with III as the extraocular movements. The numbering here is the anatomical one; the order is the one the notes use.

steps.how: Palpate the masseter and temporalis with the teeth clenched.
steps.normal: Masseter and temporalis muscles appear symmetric and strong bilaterally.

steps.how: Demonstrate the soft and sharp ends of the tool first. Eyes closed, brush a cotton wisp over the ophthalmic, maxillary and mandibular divisions and ask where it touched.
steps.normal: Sensory nerves are intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Ask the patient to mimic your expressions — raise the brows, close the eyes tightly, smile, puff the cheeks.
steps.normal: Facial nerve is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Cover one ear, eyes closed; present a sound and withdraw it to at least arm's length, asking them to say when they can no longer hear it.
steps.normal: Gross hearing is intact bilaterally.

steps.step: CN IX and X — glossopharyngeal and vagus
steps.how: Ask the patient to open the mouth and say “ahhh”; watch the soft palate, tonsillar pillars and uvula.
steps.normal: The palate and tonsillar pillars rise symmetrically with no uvular deviation.
steps.flag: The source reads “no sign of uvula deviation or tonsillar pillars rising.” The palate and pillars should rise — the abnormal findings are an asymmetric rise or a uvula that deviates away from the weak side.

steps.how: Place your hands on the shoulders and ask the patient to shrug up into them; then turn the head against resistance.
steps.normal: Spinal accessory nerve is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Ask the patient to stick out the tongue; look for deviation, atrophy and fasciculation.
steps.normal: No signs of tongue deviation.

groups.note: The source notes number these 1 to 10 in the order they are performed. Roman numerals here are the anatomical cranial nerve numbers.

steps.how: Inspect and palpate the muscles for bulk, atrophy, fasciculation and involuntary movement; then test tone and strength.
steps.normal: No signs of any atrophy, fasciculations or other involuntary movements. Muscle tone and strength of the upper extremities are intact bilaterally at +5 grade.

steps.how: Inspect and palpate the muscles for bulk, atrophy, fasciculation and involuntary movement; then test tone and strength.
steps.normal: No signs of any atrophy, fasciculations or other involuntary movements. Muscle tone and strength are intact bilaterally for the lower extremities at +5 grade.

steps.how: Demonstrate sharp and dull first. Eyes closed, test the 1st, 3rd and 5th digits and ask which they feel.
steps.normal: Upper extremity sensory function is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Demonstrate sharp and dull first. Eyes closed, test the 1st, 3rd and 5th toes and ask which they feel.
steps.normal: Lower extremity sensory function is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Eyes closed; hold the great toe at the sides, flex or extend it, and ask whether it points toward them or away.
steps.normal: Position sensation of the first toe is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Strike a 128 Hz tuning fork and place it on the dorsum of the great toe with your finger underneath, so you can feel when the vibration stops.
steps.normal: The vibration sensation in the first toe is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Name each tendon as you go: biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar and Achilles; then the plantar response (Babinski) and the abdominal reflexes above and below the umbilicus. Grade 0–4 and compare side to side.
steps.normal: DTRs +2 throughout, symmetrical and without clonus.

steps.how: Palm to dorsum to palm to dorsum on the thigh, as fast as they can.
steps.normal: Rapid alternating movements are smooth and symmetrical.

steps.how: Thumb to index, then middle, then ring, then little finger, repeating in order.
steps.normal: Finger opposition is intact bilaterally.

steps.how: Hold your fingertip out and ask them to touch it, then their nose; move your finger to the 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock positions; then back and forth between nose and finger, finally with the eyes closed.
steps.normal: Point-to-point movements are accurate with eyes open and closed.

steps.how: Supine, eyes closed; place one heel on the opposite knee and slide it down the shin to the foot, then repeat on the other side.
steps.normal: Coordination and cerebellar function is intact.

steps.how: Ask the patient to walk to the wall and back.
steps.normal: Gait is smooth, symmetrical and coordinated without any compensatory movements.

steps.how: Feet together, arms at the sides, eyes open first — there should be no sway. Then eyes closed for 30 seconds. Stand close enough to catch them.
steps.normal: Upon the Romberg test, the patient remained steady with the eyes closed.

steps.how: Both arms held out in front, palms up, eyes closed for about 30 seconds; slight pronation or downward drift is positive.
steps.normal: Negative for pronator drift bilaterally.

findings.finding: Sudden facial droop, arm drift or speech change
Positive pronator drift
Upgoing plantar response in an adult
Hyperreflexia with clonus and spasticity
Hyporeflexia with atrophy and fasciculation
Steady with the eyes open, unsteady with them closed (positive Romberg)
findings.suggests: Proprioceptive or dorsal column loss — B12 deficiency, tabes dorsalis, peripheral neuropathy

findings.finding: Unsteady with the eyes open as well
findings.suggests: Cerebellar ataxia — not a positive Romberg

findings.finding: Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia and past-pointing
findings.suggests: Cerebellar lesion, ipsilateral to the signs

findings.finding: Symmetric distal stocking-glove sensory loss
Loss of vibration and position sense before pain and temperature
Anisocoria with ptosis and anhidrosis
Fixed dilated pupil with ptosis and a down-and-out eye
Uvula deviating to one side
findings.suggests: Vagus nerve palsy — the uvula deviates away from the weak side

findings.finding: Tongue deviating on protrusion
findings.suggests: Hypoglossal lesion — the tongue deviates toward the weak side

findings.finding: Forehead spared in a facial droop
findings.suggests: Central (upper motor neuron) facial palsy rather than Bell's palsy

exams.name: Breast and Female Pelvic Exam
exams.summary: Breast and regional nodes, external genitalia, speculum and bimanual exam, and pelvic floor assessment.
exams.script: This is a sensitive exam. Explain each step before it happens, offer a chaperone and record who was present, drape so that only the area being examined is exposed, and confirm consent before starting. Stop the moment the patient asks you to.

steps.how: Patient seated: arms at the sides, then raised overhead, then hands pressed on the hips. Inspect for symmetry, dimpling, nipple retraction, discoloration and rashes.
steps.normal: Breasts have normal symmetry, without dimpling, nipple retraction, discoloration, rashes or masses.

steps.how: Patient supine with the arm overhead. Palpate in a vertical-strip pattern at three pressures over the whole breast footprint, including the tail of Spence, then compress the nipple.
steps.normal: Palpation reveals no masses or ropy areas, with no signs of nipple discharge.

steps.how: Palpate the axillary, supraclavicular, infraclavicular and epitrochlear nodes.
steps.normal: No axillary, supraclavicular, infraclavicular or epitrochlear lymphadenopathy.

steps.how: Palpate along the inguinal ligament and over the femoral triangle.
steps.normal: No inguinal or femoral lymphadenopathy.

steps.how: Inspect the mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoris, urethral meatus and introitus, separating the labia with a gloved hand.
steps.normal: Pubic hair growth and distribution is appropriate for the patient's age. Inspection of external genitalia is without lesions, edema, ulcers, scars or any nodules. Labia majora, labia minora and mons pubis are without lesions, masses or edema. No discharge or skin abnormalities noted.

steps.how: Warm and lubricate the speculum with water. Insert at an angle with downward pressure, rotate and open to bring the cervix into view. Inspect the cervix and vaginal walls; take samples if indicated.
steps.normal: Speculum exam reveals no cervical or vaginal lesions, and normal vaginal rugae.

steps.how: Two gloved fingers in the vagina, the other hand on the lower abdomen; assess uterine position, size, contour, mobility and tenderness.
steps.normal: The uterus is anteverted, non-tender and not enlarged.

steps.how: Move the cervix side to side to test for motion tenderness, then sweep each adnexa between the two hands.
steps.normal: Bimanual exam reveals no cervical motion tenderness, adnexal masses or tenderness. Ovaries are palpable without enlargement — note any adnexa surgically absent.

steps.how: Ask the patient to bear down and then to squeeze around your fingers; assess for prolapse and resting and active tone.
steps.normal: No evidence of pelvic organ prolapse, and pelvic floor muscle tone was normal.

steps.how: Indicated to assess the posterior cul-de-sac and uterosacral ligaments, a retroverted uterus, or where symptoms warrant it. Change gloves before and after.
steps.normal: Rectovaginal exam was discussed with the patient.

findings.finding: Skin dimpling, peau d'orange or new nipple retraction
Hard, fixed, irregular, non-tender mass
Unilateral spontaneous bloody nipple discharge
Eczematous, scaling nipple that does not resolve
Mobile, rubbery, well-circumscribed mass in a younger patient
Cervical motion tenderness with adnexal tenderness and fever
Unilateral adnexal mass with acute severe pain
Friable cervix with mucopurulent discharge
findings.suggests: Cervicitis — test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea

findings.finding: Fixed, retroverted uterus with nodular uterosacral ligaments
Irregularly enlarged, firm uterus
Any post-menopausal bleeding
Descent of the anterior or posterior wall or cervix on bearing down
